question: The anterior pituitary gland:

options.opa: It is part of the hypothalamus.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "regulated by hypothalamic hormones" -> "hormonal regulation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "not part of hypothalamus" -> "separate structure" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "does not release ADH and oxytocin" -> "ADH and oxytocin released by posterior pituitary" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "not formed by neurons" -> "formed by endocrine cells" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "does not directly communicate with neurohypophysis" -> "indirect communication via hypothalamus" -> 85%
analysis: The anterior pituitary gland, also known as the adenohypophysis, is primarily regulated by hormonal signals from the hypothalamus, specifically through releasing and inhibiting hormones. It does not release ADH and oxytocin; these hormones are released by the posterior pituitary gland (neurohypophysis). The anterior pituitary is not part of the hypothalamus, nor is it formed by neurons; it is composed of glandular tissue. Therefore, the correct option is that it is regulated hormonally.
